newsitem.title: USA: Taleban curbs on women could cost aid, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: Taleban curbs on women could cost aid, U.S. says.

text.p: The United States warned the new Islamic rulers in Kabul on Monday that they risked forfeiting reconstruction aid for Afghanistan if they continued to restrict women's rights.
The U.S. State Department said it had seen "some very disturbing signs" since the Taleban movement captured Kabul two weeks ago and clamped down on women working and girls going to school.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the directives "threaten to generate international isolation which would deny Afghanistan the international assistance it so badly needs after so many years of war."

The moves "are also likely to severely limit their ability to mobilise the population to dig out from over a decade of war, to rebuild the country, to establish a sense of national unity in the country," Burns told a news briefing.
The restrictions on women have been heavily reported in major newspapers in the United States, where women's rights groups are influential in domestic politics.
Burns said a plan announced last week to send a diplomat to Kabul to talk to the Taleban, which Washington has not formally recognised as the new authority in the country, had not been carried out.
But, he said: "We will seek contacts with them. We'll maintain contacts wherever we can have them -- inside or outside of Afghanistan. That just is prudent."
Burns said the United States was calling for an end to fighting which erupted between Taleban and the forces of warlord Ahmad Shah Masood, which control the Panjshir Valley north of Kabul.
"We are urging all factions -- the Taleban and others -- to stop the fighting, and to try to find some way to rebuild Afghanistan and to unify the country," he said.
